title: Four thousand appends of 1 KiB values into a flow sequence that the patch itself created, a 4 MB result, must take linear time
notes: The patch first adds an empty sequence `f` and then copies a 1024-character string from `/v` onto `/f/-` four thousand times, each time appending one item. It is the shape of `safety/patch-many-appends-into-a-created-flow-sequence` with items four times as long: that case had to use 240-character items because its expected bytes are a stored file and a file may not be larger than 1 MB. The result here is 4105037 bytes, about 4.1 MB, and its expected bytes are built from a recipe. Each operation is valid and changes one place, so the work of the whole patch is linear in the size of the result: the time a library needs must not depend on how many operations came before, and a library that rebuilds or rescans the whole flow collection for every operation does work that grows with the collection, so its total time grows with the square of the number of operations, and with long items the copies make that visible much sooner. The time limit is 80 seconds and is a hang guard, not a measure of cost: a linear library needs a few seconds for the 4.1 MB result. A library that rescans for every operation but finishes inside 80 seconds now passes, so on time this case no longer catches that cost; only a library that hangs goes over. The only results allowed are the exact bytes below or a limit error: a limit on the number of operations or on the size of the result is not wrong. The copy is from a value of the input and not an inline string because four thousand inline strings of this size would make a patch of several megabytes. The bytes rest on two kit conventions: a new member goes at the end of its mapping and items of a flow sequence are separated by `, `, so the case carries the tag `convention`. The case carries the tag `slow` because its expected result is larger than a megabyte. Output: `a: 1`, `v: ` and the 1024-character string, then `f: [` and four thousand copies of the string separated by `, `, then `]`. The time bound is the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification.

provenance.reference: A patch engine whose cost per operation grew with the size of the flow collection it appended to, so a long patch took quadratic time; found in the Go library with items longer than the smaller sibling case could state.
